directAnswer: St. Agapetus I was pope for less than a year, from 535 to 536. He traveled to Constantinople at the request of the Ostrogothic king Theodahad to try to prevent Justinian's invasion of Italy; that mission failed, but while there he deposed Patriarch Anthimus for heresy and personally consecrated his successor Menas. He died in Constantinople in April 536.

sections.h2: A Roman Archdeacon and a Library Plan
paras: Agapetus was the son of a Roman priest named Gordianus and had served as archdeacon. One of his first acts was to burn publicly the document in which Boniface II had compelled the clergy to condemn Dioscorus, a gesture of reconciliation.

With the statesman Cassiodorus, he planned a Christian school of higher learning in Rome. The project was overtaken by war, but Agapetus did establish a library at his family property on the Caelian Hill, and an inscription associated with it survives.

sections.h2: Mission to Justinian and the Deposition of Anthimus
paras: In 535, Justinian's general Belisarius was preparing to retake Italy from the Goths. King Theodahad sent Agapetus to Constantinople to negotiate peace, and the pope reportedly had to pledge church property to pay for the journey. Justinian would not call off the campaign.

In Constantinople, Agapetus found that Patriarch Anthimus had been transferred from another see and was suspected of rejecting Chalcedon. He refused communion with Anthimus, who was removed, and in March 536 consecrated Menas as patriarch. He died in Constantinople on April 22, 536; his body was returned to Rome and buried at St. Peter's. He is honored on April 22 and September 20 in the West and on April 17 in the East.

keyFacts: Pope from 535 to 536; son of the Roman priest Gordianus
Planned a Christian school with Cassiodorus and founded a library on the Caelian
Traveled to Constantinople in 536 on behalf of King Theodahad
Deposed Patriarch Anthimus and consecrated Menas
Died in Constantinople; buried at St. Peter's

faqs.question: Why did Pope Agapetus I go to Constantinople?
faqs.answer: The Ostrogothic king Theodahad sent him to persuade Emperor Justinian not to invade Italy. Justinian refused, but Agapetus used the visit to act against Patriarch Anthimus.

faqs.question: Who was Anthimus, deposed by Agapetus?
faqs.answer: Anthimus was patriarch of Constantinople and was suspected of rejecting the Council of Chalcedon. Agapetus refused communion with him, he was removed, and Agapetus consecrated Menas in his place.
